nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_000
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How many environmentally beneficial subsidies and payments were there in OECD countries as of July 2024?
nodes.answer: As of July 2024, there were 682 environmentally beneficial subsidies and payments in OECD countries.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_001
nodes.question: How many world leaders have endorsed the Leaders' Pledge for Nature, committing to the reversal of biodiversity loss by 2030?
nodes.answer: More than 90 world leaders have endorsed the Leaders' Pledge for Nature.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_002
nodes.question: Who has endorsed the Leaders' Pledge for Nature to support biodiversity recovery efforts?
nodes.answer: More than 90 world leaders have endorsed the Leaders' Pledge for Nature.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_003
nodes.question: What role do world leaders who signed the Leaders' Pledge for Nature play?
nodes.answer: Leaders who signed the Leaders' Pledge for Nature must take a special role in early implementation, leading the way by securing the necessary finance to achieve a nature-positive world by 2030.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_004
nodes.question: What role do world leaders who signed the Leaders' Pledge for Nature have?
nodes.answer: They must play a special role in leading early implementation and securing the necessary finance to achieve a nature-positive world.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_005
nodes.question: How many world leaders have endorsed the Leaders' Pledge for Nature?
nodes.answer: More than 90 world leaders have endorsed the Leaders' Pledge for Nature, committing to reverse biodiversity loss by 2030.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_006
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What impact have ECAs had on fossil fuel investments in recipient countries?
nodes.answer: ECAs have contributed billions of dollars in public finance for fossil fuels, which has helped to lock-in recipient countries to fossil fuel energy systems.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_007
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is the objective set by countries during the international climate negotiations in 2024?
nodes.answer: The objective is to mobilize USD $300 billion per year from public and private finance for developing countries by 2035.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_008
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: Which countries are mentioned in relation to export credit agencies in the context of greening portfolios?
nodes.answer: The United States and the United Kingdom are mentioned in relation to export credit agencies.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_009
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: How do ECAs have the potential to align with national climate policy objectives?
nodes.answer: As institutions controlled by national governments, ECAs can leverage their financial instruments to encourage private investment in clean energy projects.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_010
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What coalition was launched by European countries in 2021, and what was its purpose?
nodes.answer: The Export Finance for Future (E3F) coalition was launched to align export finance with international climate objectives.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_011
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What commitment did the 34 countries make by signing the Glasgow Statement in 2021?
nodes.answer: The 34 countries committed to ending public financial support for international fossil fuel projects.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_012
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: How did fossil fuel investments by ECAs from China and Japan trend from 2015 onwards?
nodes.answer: ECAs from China and Japan maintained in excess of $4 billion USD in average annual fossil fuel lending since 2015.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_013
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is the goal set by countries during the international climate negotiations in 2024 regarding financial mobilization for developing countries?
nodes.answer: The goal is to mobilize USD $300 billion per year from public and private finance for developing countries by 2035.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_014
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What coalition was launched by European countries in 2021, and what was its purpose?
nodes.answer: European countries launched the Export Finance for Future (E3F) coalition to align export finance with international climate objectives.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_015
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What commitment did 34 countries make by signing the Glasgow Statement in 2021?
nodes.answer: The 34 countries that signed the Glasgow Statement committed to ending public financial support for international fossil fuel projects.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_016
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How have fossil fuel investments by ECAs from China and Japan trended since 2015?
nodes.answer: ECAs from China and Japan have maintained in excess of $4 billion USD in average annual fossil fuel lending since 2015.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_017
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What commitments have Exlm and UKEF made regarding their portfolios?
nodes.answer: Both ECAs have committed to greening their portfolios despite mandates to promote national exports, including fossil fuels.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_018
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What issue is associated with the financial support provided by ECAs?
nodes.answer: ECAs provide billions of dollars in public finance for fossil fuels, which locks in recipient countries to fossil fuel energy systems.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_019
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is the main objective set by countries in the 2024 international climate negotiations regarding financial mobilization for developing countries by 2035?
nodes.answer: The objective set is to mobilize USD $300 billion per year from public and private finance for developing countries by 2035.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_020
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What notable agreement recognized the importance of climate finance by financial institutions, and in what year?
nodes.answer: The Paris Agreement recognized the importance of climate finance by financial institutions in 2015.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_021
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What commitment did 34 countries make by signing the Glasgow Statement in 2021?
nodes.answer: The commitment was to end public financial support for international fossil fuel projects.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_022
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What was the trend in fossil fuel investments by ECAs from 2015 according to the analysis reported in the paper?
nodes.answer: ECAs from China and Japan maintained over $4 billion USD in average annual fossil fuel lending since 2015, while Canada and South Korea averaged over $2 billion USD in annual fossil fuel spending.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|International climate agreements|Climate finance commitments_qna_023
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What commitment have both Exlm and UKEF made regarding their portfolios?
nodes.answer: Both ECAs have made commitments to green their portfolios, although with varying levels of success.
